newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India sells Apr Madras naphtha to Vitol at -$31/T.
newsitem.headline: India sells Apr Madras naphtha to Vitol at -$31/T.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has sold by tender 28,000 tonnes of high aromatic naphtha (HAN) lifting April 25-27 from Madras on the east coast to Dutch trader Vitol at a $31.00-per-tonne discount to Japanese spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis, industry sources said on Monday.
The tender closed on April 17 and bids were valid for one day.
IOC's last HAN tender from Madras, lifting March 27-29, was awarded at a much higher price of $22.28 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob.
Traders said weak gasoline prices have pressured down the price for naphtha grade used in the production of gasoline.
A tender offering 20,000 tonnes of HAN from Cochin, lifting April 30-May 2 and which closed at the same time, was cancelled due to low bids for the cargo.
IOC subsequently reissued the tender offering a larger volume of 30,000-tonnes for later lifting dates of May 6-7 which closes April 24.
